 Brandon Miller finished Saturday’s loss to the 76ers with 24 points (8-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers.
 Miller shot the ball better than he did in Friday’s loss to the Wizards, when he finished 7-of-24 from the field. This season, he’s shooting 37.7 percent from the field, nearly six percentage points lower than last season (43.5). Hopefully, the eventual returns of Coby White and Kon Knueppel will make things a bit easier for Miller by improving the quality of shots he gets in Charlotte’s offense. The Hornets play three games next week, starting with the Pistons on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brandon Miller scored 19 points (7-of-24 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, a steal, a block, and three 3-pointers in 95-79 loss to Wizards. 
 After having three straight good games in a row against the Heat, Wizards, and Pistons, he had another bad game. The Wizards did much better on containing Miller and Naz Reid in this game which allowed them to come away with a win against them. Don’t panic after he gave you several good games and he’ll have an opportunity to have a bounce back game tomorrow against the 76ers. The Hornets will not likely shoot 29.7% from the field tomorrow either. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Brandon Miller had 31 points (12-of-26 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 12 rebounds, three assists, two steals and three three-pointers against the Pistons on Wednesday. 
 After a rough first two games of the season where he combined for 24 points, Miller has scored at least 31 points in three consecutive games. His 12 rebounds were a season-high so far. Miller is still struggling with his three-pointers as he’s shot at least 30 percent from downtown in only one of the first five games. He’ll get his next chance to improve in that regard against the Wizards on the road on Friday. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 39 points (15-of-28 FGs), six rebounds, one assist, three steals, two blocks and five three-pointers in a 110-103 win over the Wizards on Monday. 
 The volume has been there all season, but the shots finally started falling for Miller in this game. That allowed him to set a new career high for scoring and score at least 30 points for a second straight game. Until Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Coby White (calf) return, Miller is going to see as many shots as he wants. He has taken 57 shots over Charlotte’s last two games and should continue to see an insane amount of usage on offense, with a trip to Detroit up next on the schedule on Wednesday. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 34 points (10-of-29 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in a 115-110 win over the Heat on Saturday. 
 Miller has been the focal point of the offense for Charlotte early on this year, which gives him a green light to shoot often. He is averaging 21.3 shot attempts per game this season, and while he still isn’t shooting efficiently, he was able to pour in the points in this one. The difference in this game was the free throw rate. He shot three total free throws in their first two games, far less than his 12 attempts in this one. Miller is going to continue to get as many shots as he wants until Kon Knueppel (hamstring) returns. He should be in for more big scoring nights, especially when his shot starts falling at a higher rate.

 Brandon Miller had six points (2-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Hawks on Friday. 
 There’s no sugarcoating it; Miller is off to a rough start to begin the season. The 23-year-old small forward had 18 points in the opener, but shot just 7-of-21 from the floor. He followed that performance up by going 2-of-14, including 1-of-11 from behind the three-point line. He’s now 4-of-25 (16 percent) from behind the arc to begin the season. Miller was an almost incomprehensible -37 in 22 minutes in the 128-81 loss to the Haws Friday. Is this rock bottom? Because it feels like it can only get better from here.

 Miller had 18 points, but struggled with efficiency as he was 7-of-21 from the field and 3-of-14 from behind the three-point line. There will be better games in his future, but with Kon Knueppel and Coby White sidelined defenses will be continue to key on Miller.

 Charlotte Hornets start Dennis Schroeder, Sion James, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid, and Moussa Diabate in season opener against the Nets 
 The Hornets have Kon Knueppel and Coby White out, so Schroeder and now Sion James will get the start with Grayson Allen coming off the bench. Even in a start, Sion James is not a great per minute producer and will likely not impact many fantasy leagues even in a start.

 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Hornets and Brandon Miller have agreed to a five-year, $209 million extension. 
 Miller’s future in Charlotte is set, as he’s agreed to a rookie-scale extension worth more than $40 million per year. With the offseason decision to trade LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, the franchise has moved forward with Miller and Kon Knueppel as cornerstones. Miller appeared in 65 games last season, averaging 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 3.1 three-pointers per game. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Brandon Miller recorded 18 points (6-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one block and four three-pointers in Sunday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 Miller was on the court on Sunday after sitting out Charlotte’s preseason opener. He led the Hornets in scoring, and he’ll be expected to do that nightly once the regular season begins. Kon Knueppel (hamstring) is not expected to be available when the season opens on October 21, which may raise Miller’s fantasy ceiling. However, to live up to those hopes, he’ll need to be more efficient. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) will miss the preseason and be re-evaluated during the first week of the regular season. 
 Given how well Knueppel played as a rookie and the Hornets’ decision to move on from LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, Friday’s news gives his 2026-27 season a brutal start. At a minimum, the runner-up for Rookie of the Year will be sidelined for four weeks, and that’s just for him to be re-evaluated. According to the Hornets, Knueppel suffered the left hamstring injury during an offseason on-court activity. His absence boosts the early-season values of Brandon Miller and Coby White while also making Grayson Allen a more viable late-round option in drafts.

 Kingston Flemings was ejected from Saturday’s game against the Pelicans with 3:04 remaining in the fourth quarter. 
 Flemings was ejected after an altercation with New Orleans’ Bryce McGowens. After McGowens blocked Flemings’ layup attempt, the rookie guard threw an elbow at the face of the Pelicans’ wing while play headed in the opposite direction. Multiple players from both teams left their benches, but no one else was ejected because the Hawks had called a timeout. Flemings finished with 12 points, two rebounds, six assists, four steals and one three-pointer.

 Naz Reid recorded 14 points (4-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and one block in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Reid has been in a bit of a funk since Charlotte’s October 24 win over the Heat. Over his last four games, the Hornets’ forward has shot 35.1 percent from the field and 21.7 percent from beyond the arc while averaging 12.8 points per game. That’s not the production fantasy managers were hoping for, especially as the Hornets continue to play without Coby White and Kon Knueppel. Hopefully, Reid can turn things around next week, with the Hornets hosting the Pistons on Monday.

 Grayson Allen accounted for 27 points (9-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and seven three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 After scoring 14 points on 4-of-18 shooting in Charlotte’s prior two games, Allen needed a night like Saturday. He shot a stellar 7-of-10 from beyond the arc, including 3-of-3 in an 11-point first quarter. The 27 points are a new season-high for Allen, who scored 20 or more in two of Charlotte’s first three games. He’ll have a higher fantasy ceiling until Coby White and Kon Knueppel are cleared to return from their injuries.

 Adem Bona recorded two points (1-of-3 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in Saturday’s win over the Hornets.
 With Joel Embiid out, Bona moved into the starting lineup on Saturday. Unfortunately, he produced little, as foul trouble limited him to 22 minutes. Jabari Walker, who played 19 minutes, picked up the slack, finishing with 12 points, six rebounds and one three-pointer. The 76ers don’t have a back-to-back in their four-game Week 3, so Bona’s opportunities are likely to be limited.

 Jaylen Brown (knee) accounted for 16 points (6-of-15 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), four rebounds, four assists and two steals in Saturday’s win over the Hornets.
 Back in action after sitting out Friday’s win over the Knicks with left patellar tendinopathy, Brown played 38 minutes against the Hornets. Even with LeBron James and Joel Embiid out, the playing time was somewhat surprising, given the injury Brown was returning from. The good news is that Philadelphia’s schedule for next week doesn’t have a back-to-back. Hopefully, that bodes well for Brown’s availability.
